title: Rise in the Full-Term Risk Premium for Deductible Decreases on Loan Transactions, NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## Measuring the rise in the full-term risk premium — deductible decrease recorded for a loan transaction (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own))

For a pending deductible decrease recorded for a loan transaction on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, the rise in the full-term risk premium on which the charge is measured is set by the first line below that holds:

| Situation on the records | Rise in the full-term risk premium |
|---|---|
| The request carries no full-term risk premium from the rating engine | No rise |
| The limit increase recorded last for the same loan closing has been billed, its endorsement charge being booked on the premium account | The request's full-term risk premium less that increase's full-term risk premium, because this request was rated on top of it |
| A re-rate credit from an applied Elevation Certificate was booked on the current term after the request was recorded | The request's full-term risk premium less the risk premium booked for the term at its start, because both figures stand on the rating basis the request was rated on |
| Otherwise | The request's full-term risk premium less the rated risk premium on the policy |

The risk premium booked for the term at its start is the risk premium charged for the current term at new business or at renewal. A re-rate credit counts here only when it is a credit on the risk premium line from an applied Elevation Certificate, posted on the current term after the date the request was recorded. The limit increase recorded last for the same loan closing is the most recently recorded coverage-increase request recording the same loan closing date as the deductible decrease; it has been billed when an endorsement charge referencing it stands on the premium account.

*Hypothetical illustration.* A request carries a full-term risk premium of 1,500.00 dollars; the rated risk premium on the policy is 1,300.00 dollars and the risk premium booked for the term at its start was 1,400.00 dollars. If the limit increase recorded last for the same loan closing has been billed and carried a full-term risk premium of 1,450.00 dollars, the rise is 50.00 dollars (1,500.00 less 1,450.00). Without it, and with no re-rate credit after the request, the rise is 200.00 dollars; with such a re-rate credit, 100.00 dollars.
